text.tspan: Architect — Human operator responsible for authoring Aurora models and
running CLI tooling (validate, render, compact) to maintain
aurora_cli — Command-line interface that discovers Aurora model homes,
validates mission-scoped models, renders Markdown + SVG views, and
aurora_shared — Shared domain library that implements model discovery,
parsing, validation, rendering, and compact export helpers for Aurora
Rendered Markdown Documentation — Per-card Markdown files and mission
executive summary emitted by the renderer into
Rendered View Diagrams — Canonical view outputs emitted under Views/:
DOT sources under Views/source and themed SVG diagrams under Views/.
Compact Agent Export — Single-file compact model export emitted as
Model Discovery and Loading — Ability to locate Aurora model homes
from a user-provided path and load all card JSON/JSJSON files into an
Model Validation — Ability to validate Aurora model invariants and
provide actionable diagnostics before any downstream rendering/export
Markdown Rendering — Ability to render human-readable Markdown
documentation for every card plus a mission-level executive summary.
View Rendering — Ability to render canonical Aurora views by
generating DOT sources and producing SVG diagrams using a
Compact Agent Export — Ability to write a compact, single-file
snapshot of a mission-scoped model for agent consumption.
Audit Version Bumping — Ability to update card audit trail versions
(patch/minor/major) and append an audit event in a deterministic,
Registry Backed Tooling — Ability to validate and render using
embedded canonical registries for card definitions, relationship
CLI Command Runner — CLI entrypoint and command dispatcher (clap
subcommands) that orchestrates discovery, validation, rendering, and
compact export workflows and reports diagnostics and summaries.
Model Discovery and Loading — Discovery and parsing layer that
locates model homes (schema-based), loads card files (JSON/JSJSON)
from disk, and builds a searchable AuroraModel index.
Validation Engine — Validator that checks structural invariants
(duplicate ids, mission presence, link targets, reachability) plus
policy checks (secret asset ownership) and relationship-matrix
Rendering Engine — Renderer that produces per-card Markdown
documentation, executive summaries, canonical view DOT sources, and
themed SVG diagrams; also writes compact agent exports.
Embedded Registries — Compile-time canonical registries for card
view definitions (canonical view set) used by validation and
Human Friendly Artifacts from Source of Truth — Avoid manual diagram
maintenance by generating rendered documentation and agent-friendly
exports directly from the authoritative Aurora card graph.
Automated Guardrails for Model Integrity — Provide deterministic,
repeatable validation and canonical registries so Aurora models
remain structurally sound (reachable, internally consistent, and
relationship-matrix compliant) before rendering or publishing.
Repository File System — Filesystem-backed store that holds Aurora
Validate Models — Validate one or more mission-scoped models
(discovered from an input path) and emit diagnostics; fail the command
Render Card Markdown — Render per-card Markdown documentation plus a
mission executive summary into a chosen output directory.
Render View Diagrams — Render canonical Aurora views by writing DOT
sources under Views/source and generating themed SVG diagrams under
Render All Artifacts — Render both card Markdown and view diagrams
for each mission-scoped model into the chosen output directory.
Write Compact Export — Write a compact, single-file mission snapshot
Bump Audit Versions — Bump model audit trail versions
(patch/minor/major). This feature is currently exposed as CLI commands
Discover and Load Models — Discover model homes from an input path and
load cards from disk into a mission-splittable AuroraModel structure.
Embedded Canonical Registries — Provide embedded registries for
card definitions, relationship definitions, and view definitions for
Graphviz DOT Renderer — External executable interface for rendering
Graphviz DOT into a layout used to generate themed SVG views (default:
CLI Tooling — Provide CLI tooling capable of managing, rendering,
Discover and Load Models — The tooling SHALL discover one or more
Aurora model homes from an input path (file, model-home directory, or
ancestor directory) and load all card files under each model home.
Discovery is schema-based (presence of Aurora.schema.*), supports a
direct child 'aurora/' folder, and bounds directory walking (max depth)
Validate Models and Emit Diagnostics — The tooling SHALL validate
loaded models for core invariants (unique ids, at least one Mission,
valid link targets, reachability from the mission root) and SHALL emit
SHALL fail the command when errors are present and SHOULD still surface
Render Card Markdown — The tooling SHALL render per-card Markdown
documentation and a mission executive summary into a user-specified
output directory. Rendered files SHOULD mirror the source card layout
(card-type subfolders) and MUST be produced only after the model
Render View Diagrams — The tooling SHALL render view diagrams (DOT
sources plus SVG output) for the canonical view set. Rendering MUST use
a Graphviz-compatible DOT renderer (default 'dot') and SHOULD allow
overriding the executable via environment configuration
Write Compact Agent Export — The tooling SHALL generate a single-file
compact export suitable for agent consumption (AGENT-<MISSION_ID>.jsjson
by default) by removing non-essential fields (e.g., $schema, audit trail
metadata) while preserving the card graph structure.
Bump Model Audit Versions — The CLI SHOULD support bumping model audit
trail versions (patch, minor, major) with deterministic edits to
affected cards and an appended audit history entry. The current
aurora_cli surface exposes bump commands but does not yet implement
Embed Canonical Registries — The tooling SHALL embed canonical
registries for card types, relationship verbs, and view definitions so
validation and rendering can operate deterministically without
depending on external instruction files at runtime.
